newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO says Hamas militant still at large.
newsitem.headline: PLO says Hamas militant still at large.

text.p: A leader of the Islamic militant group Hamas, previously reported under Palestinian Authority arrest, is still at large, Palestinian Attorney General Khaled al-Qidra said on Sunday.

"There is a warrant for the arrest of Dr Ibrahim al-Makadmeh. He is still at large," al-Qidra told Reuters, a day after a Hamas source reported the militant leader had been arrested in the wake of a Tel Aviv suicide bombing on Friday.
Makadmeh, a leader of a Hamas military wing, was released from prison by Palestinian President Yasser Arafat earlier this month.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had accused Arafat of tacitly giving Hamas a "green light" to strike against the Jewish state by freeing Makadmeh and other militants arrested last year after suicide bombers killed 59 people in Israel.
A Hamas source said the group mistakenly reported that Makadmeh had been arrested on Friday.

"Since the Palestinian police have raided his home several times, the family said he was arrested. But we have found out that the police are looking for him," said the source, who refused to be identified.
Hamas sources refused to comment on whether Makadmeh, a dentist by profession, had gone underground.
"We are searching for him and he must surrender himself to security forces," a Palestinian intelligence official said.
After the bombing, in which three Israeli women were killed, Makadmeh told a rally in the Gaza Strip that only bombs could stop Israel's settlement drive in land occupied in the 1967 Middle East war.

The intelligence official, who refused to be identified, said Palestinian forces had not been ordered to launch mass arrests of militants despite Israel's demand the PLO crack down on Hamas and other groups.
"We have no instructions for arrests," the official said.
